title: HDFC Bank shares rise for third day, gain 12% from 52-week low - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
FILE PHOTO: HDFC Bank shares extended their gains for a third consecutive session on Thursday, recovering 12.36 per cent from their 52-week low. | Photo Credit: Dado Ruvic

HDFC Bank shares rose 2.08 per cent to ₹752.00 on the NSE by 12.05 pm Thursday, up ₹15.30 from Wednesday’s close of ₹736.70, marking a third straight session of gains. The stock opened strongly at ₹760.00, hit an intraday high of ₹762.70, and held above ₹749.10 on the downside.

The three-session rally has lifted the stock 12.36 per cent from the 52-week low of ₹669.20 touched on October 28, recovering significant ground lost during a turbulent fortnight marked by back-to-back leadership changes. Total market capitalisation rose to ₹11,59,977.21 crore. Traded volume reached 323.52 lakh shares worth ₹2,441.80 crore, with deliverable quantity at 66.44 per cent.

Selling pressure, however, remained extreme — sellers accounted for 85.79 per cent of total order quantity against buyers at just 14.21 per cent, the highest sell-side dominance in this week’s sessions, suggesting sustained distribution at higher levels even as the price continues to climb. The P/E ratio expanded to 14.19, with the adjusted figure at 13.99.

Bank Nifty provided strong sectoral tailwinds, opening sharply higher near 57,103 and trading above its 20-, 50-, 100-, and 200-day EMAs — a broad technical alignment not seen in recent months. The index traded at 55,913, with resistance at 56,950–57,330 and support at 55,870–55,700.

The stock’s one-week return now stands at 10.11 per cent, against the Nifty 50’s 6.37 per cent, though the year-to-date loss of 24.09 per cent remains steep.
